record.paper_title: Some open problems in low dimensional dynamical systems
record.original_question: Determine whether there exist two irreducible algebraic curves of degrees n and m with n + m > 4, each containing an oval, such that the associated Poncelet map is well defined and conjugate to a rotation of the circle.

evidence.quote: Problem 23. Are there two irreducible algebraic curves of degreesn andm, withn+m> 4, having each one of them an oval, for which the Poncelet’s map P is well deﬁned and it is conjugated to a rotation of the circle?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let C and D be two irreducible real algebraic curves in the real projective (or affine) plane, of degrees n and m respectively, each containing an oval (a smooth, closed, convex connected component of its real locus). Given a point p on the oval of C, draw a tangent line to the oval of D; under suitable genericity assumptions this line meets the oval of C at a second point p'. The map P sending p to p' is called the (generalized) Poncelet map associated with the pair (C, D); when P closes up consistently it defines a self-map of the oval of C (topologically a circle).

Question: Do there exist two irreducible algebraic curves of degrees n and m with n + m > 4, each carrying an oval, for which the associated Poncelet map P is well defined on the oval of C and is topologically conjugate to a rigid rotation of the circle?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not turn up a published resolution of this question. The problem appears to remain open as posed, but available evidence is insufficient to confirm its current status definitively.
